texte: Write down three sounds you can hear right now, from the nearest to the farthest.
Describe the light in the room without using the word "light".
plus_petit: Just say where it comes from.

texte: Pick up something within reach. Write its weight, its temperature, the sound it makes when you put it down.
Look out of the nearest window and write down the first thing that moves.
plus_petit: Or the first thing that stays still.

texte: Describe a mug, a glass or a bottle as if nobody had ever seen one before.
Empty a pocket, a bag or a drawer on paper, in the order things come out.
Write the route from your front door to your bed. Count the steps if you like.
plus_petit: Just the door and the bed.

texte: Describe a smell you met today: where, when, what it was like.
plus_petit: Naming the place is already plenty.

texte: Log today's weather like a station report: sky, wind, temperature, ground.
Describe your shoes for someone who has to find them in a crowded station.
Watch a plant, a tree or a stain on a wall for one minute, then write it down.
Describe a sound that repeats (fridge, clock, rain, traffic) and its rhythm.
Where is your body touching something right now (chair, floor, clothes, phone)? Write each point of contact, one per line.
Write what you last ate, with the precision of a chemist or a chef.
Describe your hands right now: where they are, what they touch, what they did today.
Describe an everyday social rule (saying hello, queuing, giving a present) the way a visiting anthropologist would.
Someone is waiting for a bus that never comes. Write what they do with their hands.
plus_petit: Write the time on the board.

texte: A letter arrives twenty years late. Write the address on the envelope, then its first line.
A lighthouse is lit for the last time. The keeper packs away one single thing. What is it?
Two people share an umbrella that is too small. Nobody speaks. Describe the rain.
plus_petit: The sound of rain on the fabric.

texte: A bakery at five in the morning, before opening.
A cleaning robot finds an object it cannot file. Write its storage label.
plus_petit: The name it gives the object.

texte: Someone wakes up in a house they don't know. Write the first minute, only what they see.
A character has just heard important news. Say nothing about what they feel: write only what their hands, feet and eyes do for one minute.
A librarian notices that one book always comes back with the same page folded down. Which page?
A night train stops in the middle of nowhere. The guard announces: "…". Finish the announcement.
Someone is repainting a door. Describe the colour before and the colour after.
A grandmother and her grandson peel vegetables without talking. Describe only their movements and the sounds of the kitchen.
A character packs a suitcase for a trip they may never take. List what goes in.
A family arrives in a country whose alphabet they can't read yet. Write the first three words a child learns to recognise on the signs.
Describe the kitchen of a place you once lived. Where was the sink? Where was the window?
The first address you knew by heart. What was across the street?
Something you owned as a child and no longer have: its size, its colour, where it was kept.
A journey you made hundreds of times. Three landmarks along the way.
A dish someone used to make often. Write the recipe, even roughly.
A precise sound from a precise year (a ringtone, a theme tune, an engine). Where did you hear it?
The oldest object in the room. Where did it come from? How long has it been there?
The shoes lined up by the door of a family home: how many pairs, whose, in what order.
Write a sentence of exactly ten words.
Write three sentences that all begin with "There is".
Write a sentence without the letter "e".
List blue things that are neither the sky nor the sea.
Write instructions for a very simple object: a spoon, a door, a button.
Write a small ad: lost, found, or free to a good home.
Start with "I remember" and add one tiny fact. Repeat, if you feel like it.
Write a sentence containing a number, a colour and a place name.
Tell yesterday in five words.
Invent the title of a book that doesn't exist, then its back-cover blurb in two sentences.

Carry on from this opening, with a character of your own: "It is a truth universally acknowledged, that a single man in possession of a good fortune must be in want of a wife." (Jane Austen, Pride and Prejudice, 1813)
Carry on from this opening: "Call me Ishmael." (Herman Melville, Moby-Dick, 1851)
plus_petit: Write the narrator's real name instead.

texte: Carry on from this opening, somewhere else: "There was no possibility of taking a walk that day." (Charlotte Brontë, Jane Eyre, 1847)

Answer this opening in your own way: "Whether I shall turn out to be the hero of my own life, or whether that station will be held by anybody else, these pages must show." (Charles Dickens, David Copperfield, 1850)
plus_petit: Name who else might be the hero.

texte: Carry on from this opening: "It is very seldom that mere ordinary people like John and myself secure ancestral halls for the summer." (Charlotte Perkins Gilman, The Yellow Wallpaper, 1892)
plus_petit: Describe one room of the house.

source.reference: Charlotte Perkins Gilman, The Yellow Wallpaper, 1892

texte: Carry on from this opening: "Mrs Dalloway said she would buy the gloves herself." (Virginia Woolf, Mrs Dalloway in Bond Street, 1923)

source.reference: Virginia Woolf, Mrs Dalloway in Bond Street, 1923

texte: Carry on from this opening: "And after all the weather was ideal." (Katherine Mansfield, The Garden Party, 1922)

Write a sentence on the same pattern, for your own narrator: "In my younger and more vulnerable years my father gave me some advice that I've been turning over in my mind ever since." (F. Scott Fitzgerald, The Great Gatsby, 1925)

source.reference: F. Scott Fitzgerald, The Great Gatsby, 1925

texte: Write a clumsy sentence on purpose, as wobbly as you can. Nobody will ever grade it.
Describe what you would do with one completely free hour, with no need to be useful.
If a feeling is around, describe it as weather, an object or a temperature. If not, write "nothing in particular" and describe the room instead: both are complete answers.
Write one sentence for whoever opens this notebook in ten years, even if that's you.
plus_petit: Today's date and one thing you can see.
